component.name: SCANCORE
component.summary: Read comics and novels and watch anime

description.p: SCANCORE brings comics, web novels and anime together in a native desktop app. Read from your files and the sources you choose, keep a personal library and reading history, and download chapters for offline reading.
Your library and settings stay on your device. An optional account can sync library and reading progress with scancore.onl.
SCANCORE is also available for Android, with a phone-focused interface and touch controls.

ul.li: Read manga, manhwa, webtoons and novels with adjustable reading controls.
Browse anime on AniList and play episodes from your sources inside the app.
Keep AniList, MyAnimeList and Comick up to date as you read and watch.
Track series in one library, with history, progress and chapter downloads.
Use light, dark and black themes, keyboard shortcuts and backup and restore.

screenshot.caption: Library and recommendations on the home screen
Read comics in a continuous reader

description.p: Edit, delete and report comments; deleting a comment and unfollowing a friend work again.
A series moved to another source stays there: Continue reading no longer shows the old source again after a sync.

Signing out takes your library off the device so a new account starts empty, Continue opens the chapter where you stopped, browser checks block redirecting ads and pop-ups, MangaDex finds adult titles when allowed, and replies to your comments arrive as notifications.
A new Latest page: this week's trending comics, anime and novels on scancore.onl, and the newest comments and reviews as they are posted.

Short swipes on phones scroll instead of tapping what is under the finger. Downloading an episode no longer closes the app, anime can be downloaded from their own page, and Aniyomi backups bring anime in as anime.

Forgot your password? Get a 6-digit code by email and choose a new password without leaving the app. Passwords from known data breaches are refused, and the sign-in form moves smoothly between its steps.
Copy, save or share a comic page from the reader, and pin the extensions and sources you use most so they come first.

Anime fixes: Continue lists every show you are still watching, anime opened from the Library load their page again, covers that AniList replaced come back, and a long list of servers in the player folds into one menu.

Echo music extensions under Music, series and anime pages that keep their place when you switch between chapters, reviews and discussion, no crash report when the Android app closes itself, and a strip reader scroll bar that follows the page.

CloudStream extensions under Anime, your own OPDS catalogues and Jellyfin server as sources, FB2 and MOBI books, a home-screen widget on Android, music in the system's media controls, a redone Wrapped and a steadier strip reader.

Music: anime openings and endings from AnimeThemes, your own music files and music extensions, with synced lyrics you can tap to jump to, a queue, a mini player that keeps going while you read, and the song's video beside its words.
Fixes the Android player's picture freezing when the next episode starts on some phones.

A new welcome: real covers, a choice of comics, novels and anime that the tabs follow, Mihon, Tachiyomi, Komikku, Aniyomi and LNReader libraries brought over in one step, a live preview of the look, and a sample chapter to try the reader on.
Comick's search filters on the Comics page (genres and tags to include or leave out, status, type, years, rating and more), and Anime4K's Best sharpening drawn correctly on Linux.
Back closes the anime player's own menu before the player, and goes to the previous step on the welcome screens. Sources show their catalogue right below the source chips.

Friends and lists shared by link, reactions on a page, two readers side by side, natural voices and page translation that work offline on the computer, sharper downloaded scans, key profiles per series, and glass menus.
Fixes pages that could stay empty in the Retro look, such as Settings.
Fixes pages and readers that could open empty in 2.12.1, and makes Settings and the player work with a TV's remote. Includes everything from 2.12.1.

The Windows Phone look is now called Retro, and its animations stay smooth while pages load. Translation reads a comic as one story and has a language picker in the reader. Fixes a player freeze after the next episode.

A Windows Phone (Metro) look, comic pages translated over the page, watch parties, your own Komga, Kavita and Suwayomi servers as sources, webtoons that run on into the next chapter, auto-scroll, a rebuilt read-aloud, novels as EPUB, and scrolling and flings that keep up with your fingers.

Mihon and Komikku downloads read where they are, as downloads of your library's chapters, an anime player that no longer turns into an ad site on Android, a comic progress bar with several looks and your own colours, web views for extensions on computers, easier extension updates and browsing, and extensions in All sources search.

Built-in lists you can rename, reorder and hide, Komikku and TachiyomiSY backups, an anime player that no longer closes when pressed, with one settings panel, fit modes and touch gestures, smoother scrolling on slow phones, and chapters from newer Keiyoushi extensions.

Mihon backups that bring back everything (lists in order, history, pages, chapter and reader settings, repositories and extensions), Kagane as a built-in source, a chapter grid with Volumes, Chapters and Extras tabs, hold-to-zoom in the comic reader, and fixes for extensions on computers and settings lost on restart.

Your own library lists, a preferred quality and audio (dubs) for anime, a quality menu in the player, the screen kept on while watching and reading, one scrolling chapter list, and extensions working again on computers.
Android status bar icons follow SCANCORE's theme instead of the phone's light or dark mode.

Anime keeps working while AniList is down, with Kitsu and ani.zip standing in. Sharper comic pages and webtoons, a full screen button in the player, and an image cache that keeps what you are reading.
Extension anime plays again, including servers that disguise their videos as pictures, and AniZone loads on desktop.
The anime spotlight can be swiped: the slide follows your finger and a quick flick changes the title.

On phones the readers' top bar no longer slides over the status bar when it hides, both readers draw under the status bar with their controls below it, and the novel's title gets its own row under the reader's buttons.

Settings → Sources opens and scrolls quickly again, listing the built-in sources a dozen at a time with a search, and other long lists (source chips, Add a section, moving several series, Library health, comments and reviews) only build what is on screen.

Read from looks a title up on the built-in sources only and asks your extensions one at a time when you pick one; its list scrolls and opens from the bottom on phones. Buttons and choices no longer spill out of their cards on phones, a startup crash on systems whose Qt hashes through OpenSSL 3 is fixed, and the cookies of scancore.onl and your sync server are never shared with extensions.

One story across comic, novel and anime: a series page shows its other forms with your progress, anime pages say where the comic or novel goes on after each season (suggested and voted on by readers), and Home offers to continue the story. Upcoming shows what comes out next in your library, Library health finds sources that stopped and series saved twice, and Kitsu, MangaUpdates and Bangumi join the trackers. Titles can be looked up on your extensions, and Home sections can be removed or added from extensions.

Adding a second repository no longer closes SCANCORE, and repository links work in every form (GitHub pages, owner/name, raw folders, LNReader plugin lists, several at once). AniList connects inside the app, watching updates trackers reliably, Continue watching shows the right episode and leaves out planned and finished series, and crash reports can be shared.

SCANCORE Wrapped for your year in comics, novels and anime; live progress between your devices and Continue on another device; anime downloads; casting to Chromecasts and smart TVs; opening episodes in another player; subtitle style and Anime4K sharpening; an e-ink mode; SCANCORE's own video player in the Flatpak; and the interface in Polish, Thai, Filipino and Hindi.

Keiyoushi extensions run again, Cloudflare checks pass by themselves as in Mihon (with one tap at most when a site insists), repositories can be added without installing anything and extensions install in the background, installed extensions can be searched, and opening a check no longer closes SCANCORE on some Linux computers.

Move series to another source, update rules and automatic downloads, chapter bookmarks and filters, incognito mode and an app lock, a colour filter, split spreads, tap zones and volume keys in the comic reader, exact restores of Aniyomi and LNReader backups, themes that carry your whole look, AVIF images, and faster long novel chapters.
"Read from" on Windows finds series under the other names a source lists them by again, and Kakao Page joins the Korean comic sources with every episode it shows without an account.

Comics, novels and anime from the extensions you already use, a built-in video player, pages you arrange yourself, the interface in fourteen more languages and sources in your language, including official webtoon editions in eight languages. A library per media with categories and favourites, notifications, read aloud for novels, full-screen reading, backups for Mihon, a licences screen and a much faster app.

Comics in Spanish from MangaDex (Español), ManhwaWeb, InManga, LeerCapitulo and MangaOni. Settings shows each source's language and can keep "All sources" to one, and the welcome screen starts with the interface language. Titles match with or without accents, Spanish chapter numbers are read correctly, and MangaDex comics are tracked on AniList and MyAnimeList by the ids MangaDex gives. Episodes open again from an anime's page, and on Android the keyboard's Enter key searches.

Comics are found through Comick's catalogue, with its trending, popular and new shelves on the Comics page. Comments and reviews from scancore.onl now appear in the app for comics, novels and anime, and you can post them. Chapter lists show ten chapters at a time with a search, the comic reader's page bar is back at the left edge, and creating a scancore.onl account asks for an access code.

Adds an Activity page with your year in review, sync through your own server, WebDAV or a folder, comics and books from your own files, search through Comick's catalogue, AniList, MyAnimeList and Comick tracking, library imports from Mihon, AniList, MyAnimeList and Comick, two-page spreads, page trimming and zoom in the comic reader, a theme gallery, and Spanish, French, Brazilian Portuguese and Indonesian. Also fixes parts of the app working on separate copies of the library and account.

Anime plays on every desktop again, including in the Flatpak. Adds custom themes with a colour wheel, background pictures and GIFs, transparency and shareable .sct theme files, navigation styles, changeable shortcuts, a reorganised Settings, a Continue card on Home, library sorting and recent searches, with lighter sync and many fixes.
Improves comic and novel reading controls, Android navigation, phone layouts and account progress sync. Adds redesigned settings, faster resume, network retries and configurable image cache size.
First Flatpak-ready release of SCANCORE, with comics, novels and anime, a local library, reading history, offline downloads, and the latest desktop and phone layout improvements.
